skill.name: vercel-react-best-practices
skill.description: Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React or Next.js code with Vercel's official performance rules for async work, bundles, server paths, renders, and JavaScript hot spots.
whenToUse: Reviewing React or Next.js code for performance regressions before landing it
Refactoring async data flows that may serialize independent work into waterfalls
Reducing client bundle cost from broad imports, heavy components, or eager third-party code
Checking server component, server action, cache, serialization, and after() patterns in a Next.js app
Optimizing frequent re-renders, long list rendering, hydration behavior, or expensive JavaScript loops

keyConcepts.explanation: The skill organizes Vercel performance guidance by impact. Critical waterfall and bundle rules come before server-side, client-fetching, rerender, rendering, JavaScript, and advanced patterns.

Each rule has a stable prefix such as async-, bundle-, server-, rerender-, or rendering-. Those identifiers let an agent load the narrow reference file that matches the problem instead of applying vague performance advice.
Independent operations should start together where possible. The rule set covers Promise.all, deferred awaits, API-route promise scheduling, dependency-aware parallelism, and Suspense boundaries.
The bundle rules cover barrel imports, static analyzability, dynamic imports, deferred third-party code, conditional modules, and preloading. They target both dev latency and production load cost.

Server rules cover server action authentication, per-request deduplication with React.cache for non-fetch work, cross-request caching, RSC serialization, static I/O hoisting, parallel fetching, and non-blocking after() work.

The lower-priority sections still capture common regressions: unstable effect dependencies, unnecessary rerenders, long-list rendering, hydration handling, repeated lookups, DOM batching, and idle-time work.

apiReference.purpose: Install the Vercel React performance skill by its public skills.sh slug.
Read the detailed reference for a focused rule after the quick-reference table points to the relevant category.
Representative critical rule: collapse independent waits into one concurrent step.
apiReference.example:
const [user, posts, comments] = await Promise.all([
  fetchUser(),
  fetchPosts(),
  fetchComments()
])

apiReference.purpose: Representative server rule: deduplicate non-fetch async work during a request, such as auth or database reads.

gotchas: This is an agent rule set, not a profiler; verify performance-sensitive claims with measurements when the change matters
Read the targeted rule file before applying a shorthand identifier because some rules are framework-specific
React.cache uses argument identity; inline object arguments can miss the deduplication the rule is trying to create
Bundle advice depends on whether the bundler can analyze imports; Next.js package import optimization and direct imports are not interchangeable everywhere
Lower-priority micro-optimizations should not distract from critical waterfalls and bundle regressions
